name: ai-decision-authority
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and other agents the repo supports
short: Decides which marketing tasks an AI agent can run alone, which need a human to approve, and which a human should own.
what: Before you let an agent act on a marketing or go-to-market task without review, this skill asks three questions: can it be corrected if wrong, who sees it, and how often does it happen. Then it puts the task in one of three zones: AI-primary, collaborative or human-primary. Each zone has a rule, and it always names what breaks if the task is put in the wrong zone. It works for one decision or a list of thirty workflows.
who: Marketing leads and ops people writing an AI review policy or deciding what an agent may send on its own. If you don't run AI on marketing work, skip it.
needs: A coding agent that loads skills

steps.title: In Claude Code: add the marketplace
Install the marketing bundle
steps.text: Most skills in this repo ship inside a domain bundle. This one lives in the marketing folder.

steps.title: Other agents
steps.text: Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and others can use the open-source `skills` installer.

try.label: From the SKILL.md
try.text: Ask whether your agent can draft the weekly newsletter and schedule it. The skill's own example splits that into free drafting and a human-gated send, and reports reversibility, exposure, frequency, the zone and the rule.

watch: The framework comes from one enterprise deployment across 16 product launches. The skill says it was observational, not a controlled study, and its 70% figure may not transfer to you.
It gives advice and changes no permissions on its own.
